title: A warm evening without applause
meaning: The beauty you create can give quiet pleasure, even when the wish for immediate reassurance calls for a more visible response.
text: Shared pleasure need not be loud. In Svadhisthana, the Empress in the physical position helps you make something enjoyable: cooking, arranging a beautiful setting or choosing a familiar flavour. The Lovers in energy make an invitation vulnerable when it carries a wish for immediate reassurance of mutual affection. The Hermit in emotions suggests a quieter response. You may need time to listen to an impression and understand precisely what you enjoyed. A generous offering and a feeling still finding its own words can therefore move at different speeds.

Suppose you arrange a bouquet together from flowers bought at the market. You match colours, change the vase and step back to look. Afterwards, simply sitting beside each other feels pleasant. **Quiet enjoyment can still be shared.** A pause beside the finished bouquet does not cancel your participation in making it. There is time to notice an individual flower, recall an amusing discovery at the market and gradually name what you both remember.

Things become harder if silence is read as indifference. You might decorate something else, offer another pleasure and try to obtain unmistakable delight. That expectation can invite further withdrawal: hearing your own response becomes difficult when the correct reaction seems awaited. Efforts to bring you closer then become tiring. Recognising different ways of enjoying yourselves leaves warmth and space for pleasure to become clear.
